Treatment of persons suffering from Schizophrenia comprises of behavioral therapies, psycho therapies, counseling for prevention of substance abuse if substance […]
contentHtml:
Mental Health Issues we address

Our experienced Mental Health Professionals are experts in their respective domains and strive for excellence in their approach.

Treatment of Schizophrenia

Schizophrenia is a long-term condition that affects how a person thinks, feels and perceives reality, with symptoms such as hallucinations, delusions and disorganised thinking. Treatment combines antipsychotic medication, psychotherapy and family support, with rehabilitation and counselling to prevent relapse and, where substance use is also present, to address that too.

Click here

Treatment of Bipolar Disorder

Bipolar Disorder comprises of three distinct mood states of mania, depression & hypomania, and is ideally treated with mood stabilizers, anti-psychotics & anti-depressants along with psychotherapy which involves counseling.

Click here

Treatment of OCD

OCD is characterized by irrelevant thoughts and fears (obsessions), which lead to repetitive behavior (compulsion). Treatment includes Talk Therapy, medication or both. Deep brain stimulation (DBS) & Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) may be used in treatment resistant cases.

Click here

Alcohol De-Addiction

At IPD units such as rehabilitation centres /psychiatric hospitals, the withdrawal symptoms like seizures, tremors and hallucinations which occur after abstinence, are taken care of. During recovery, medicines are administered. Group therapy(AA,etc.) may also be used.

Click here

Tobacco de-addiction

Patients are expected to quit cold turkey or with nicotine replacement therapy after detoxification. The addicted patients usually stay for 3 to 6 months at a rehabilitation centre or a psychiatric/mental hospital to completely overcome all tobacco withdrawal symptoms.

Click here

Cocaine de-addiction

The treatment of cocaine addiction begins with a week-long detoxification. After that, the person struggling with cocaine addiction is made to stay cocaine-abstinent for 30-90 days, even longer in some cases, till all withdrawal symptoms and probability of relapse have assuaged.

Click here

Heroin de-addiction

Both pharmacological and behavioral therapies can benefit persons who are struggling with addiction to heroin. Cognitive Behavioral TherAapy and Contingency management are two behavioral therapies which have been used successfully to treat heroin addiction.

Click here

Smack de-addiction

As in cases of heroin addiction, detoxification followed by Medication Assisted Treatment and behavioral therapies can benefit persons who are struggling with addiction to smack, which is a form of heroin. Both CBT & Contingency Management behavior therapies can be used in such cases too.

Click here

Brown Sugar de-addiction

Brown sugar is an adulterated form of heroin, also called smack. Treatment is similar to treatment of smack/heroin addiction. Withdrawal symptoms experienced during treatment include aggravated violent behavior, symptoms of influenza (runny nose) & nausea.

Click here

Cough Syrup de-addiction

It is advisable for persons struggling with addiction to cough syrup to get admitted in an IPD setup such as a rehabilitation centre or a psychiatric/mental hospitals as the treatment shall require medication and a detailed comprehensive therapy program, which can be better administered in controlled settings.

Click here

Whitener / Spirit de-addiction

School going children have easy access to inhalants present in whiteners & spirits, which are commonly available at stationery stores as correction fluid, thinners, ink removers and glue. It is possible to treat this addiction by long-term counseling, anti-depressants & anti-craving drugs.

Click here

Prescription Drugs’ de-addiction

People who are addicted to prescription drugs such as painkillers, opiates, stimulants and/or barbiturates need to go through a medical detoxification program, during which they may experience withdrawal symptoms like seizures, flu-like symptoms when the dosage of the concerned drug is tapered. Relapse prevention is a major challenge.

Click here

Treatment of Personality Disorders

Therapies such as cognitive behavioral therapy, group therapy & psychoeducation are leveraged in order to treat personality disorders of all three clusters, i.e., cluster A, cluster B & cluster C

Click here

Treatment of Dementia

Dementia is a cluster of conditions characterized by impairment of at least two brain functions, such as loss of memory and judgment. Therapies leveraged are Rehabilitation & Occupational Therapies. Medication to be administered is cognition-enhancing medicine.

Click here

Treatment of Mania

Mania is characterized by highly elevated and excitable mood states for prolonged periods of time. Mood stabilizers & Anti-psychotics are the most commonly administered medicines for treatment of Mania. Episodes of Mania are usually exhibited by patients suffering from Bipolar Disorder

Click here

Treatment of Depression

Depression is a disorder of emotional state that involves persistent feeling of despair and loss of interest in everyday activities. It can be treated by Talk Therapy or medication (administration of anti-depressants) or using a combination of both

Click here

Treatment of Anxiety and related Disorders

Anxiety is associated with feelings of fear & worry which meddle with performance of routine chores in an individual’s everyday life. Anxiety disorders include OCD, PTSD and panic attacks. Anxiety and associated disorders can be treated using medication, CBT, Meditation and Psychotherapy.

Click here

Treatment of Stress & related Disorders

Stress involves failure to recover from being witness to or having experienced a traumatic or petrifying event. CBT, ERP,ET, Eye movement desensitization and reprocessing along with appropriate medication can help in treatment of stress and associated disorders.

Click here

Treatment of Alzheimer’s Disease

Alzheimer’s Disease is a progressive disease which deteriorates memory and compromises crucial functions of the brain. Though there is no cure for this disease, cognition enhancing medication, management strategies and self care (physical exercise) may temporarily alleviate symptoms.

Click here

Treatment of Dissociative disorders

The most common Dissociative disorders include Dissociative amnesia, Dissociative Identity Disorder & Depersonalization-Derealization Disorder. Psychotherapies such as talk therapy, counseling or psychosocial therapy are administered for treatment of dissociative disorders. Antidepressants, anti-anxiety medications or antipsychotic drugs may be prescribed by psychiatrists for treatment of associated symptoms.

Click here

Treatment of Somatic Symptom and Related Disorders

Somatic symptom disorder is characterized by the suffering person emphasizing heavily on physical symptoms such as exhaustion and soreness of a muscle; which leads to a lot of emotional anguish and problems carrying out routine tasks. Psychotherapies such as CBT and Family Therapy can be implemented in such cases to tackle the symptoms in addition to administration of anti-depressants.

Click here

Treatment of Feeding and Eating Disorders

For people with anorexia nervosa, effective treatment must always include regular and adequate nutrition. People with bulimia nervosa or binge eating disorder may need to lose some weight to avoid or to overcome medical problems. Psychological treatments include: Family Therapy, CBT, interpersonal psychotherapy & psychodynamic psychotherapy.

Click here

Treatment of Sleep – Wake Disorders

Tackling and rectifying irregular sleep-wake patterns of the body focuses on increasing the stimulation to reset the sleep clock in the brain. The primary objective is to have one long sleep phase during night and one long awake phase during day time. Light treatment is one way to help a destabilized body clock. Behavioral counseling may also be beneficial.

Click here

Treatment of Neuro-cognitive Disorders

Neuro-cognitive Disorders, often collectively referred to as Organic Brain Syndrome, are a set of conditions which lead to mental impairment. Treatment involves giving time for the injured brain to fully recuperate, followed by administration of pain killers and antibiotics. Occupational therapy & Physical therapy are also leveraged to treat such disorders.

Click here

At times, you or someone you care for may require emergency mental healthcare interference. If you or someone you care about requires such emergency care, call 8800000255 or 7707070002 for assistance from Tulasi Health Care.

contentHtml:
Frequently Asked Questions

DO I NEED REHABILITATION TREATMENT FOR MY ADDICTION?

All the people suffering from addiction do not require admission to a Rehab Centre; few cases can be dealt in the OPD. If the patient understands his problem and is motivated to work on them sincerely there is a chance he may improve by seeing his therapist on a regular basis, the support groups like AA and NA are also helpful in motivating the patient to give up his addiction.

WHY ADDICTION IS CALLED A DISEASE?

Addiction takes a form of disease because it is beyond the control of the patient. It is like any other viral fever which has relapses and treatment is required to overcome it. There is no element of self control or will power which can control it. It is only when the patient comes out of denial and is motivated to bring a change in himself with the help of family, psychiatrist and psychologist and support groups that he is able to beat it.

IS THE REHABILITATION PROGRAM SAME FOR EVERY ONE?

No, the program is different for different people. It is generally determined by severity of the disease and understanding and motivation of the client. Program is customized depending upon age, sex, religion, cultural beliefs and mental status of the patient.

DO THE MEDICINES WHICH ARE USED FOR TREATMENT HAVE AN ADDICTIVE POTENTIAL?

No, medicines are used keeping in mind that these people are predisposed to abusing even the prescription drugs. The medicines used for withdrawals are gradually tapered and patient is only maintained on medicines that are essential for his physical and mental well being.

WHAT IS THE OPTIMUM DURATION OF TREATMENT?

That is again dependent on the severity of the disease, insight about the disease and willingness to work on the problems. A good treatment is for 12 weeks but can be shortened or lengthened according to the individuals needs. But anything short of 6 weeks is not recommended.

IS THE TREATMENT COVERED UNDER HEALTH INSURANCE?

Mental illness is covered under health insurance. So, if your particular health insurance policy covers mental illness, you can claim re-imbursement of the treatment expenses from your insurance provider. Please contact your health insurance provider for details. Policy holders of SBI General Insurance & Future Generali Insurance can avail cashless treatment for mental illness and as per their particular policy conditions.

WHAT ARE THE CHANCES OF RELAPSE?

There is 60% to 70 % chance that your patient will remain clean after the first treatment. Relapse does not indicate that the treatment has failed it simply implies that the patient requires another intervention and change in approach in dealing with addiction. Family and therapist should not give up on the patient.

DOES THIS TREATMENT CATER TO THE MEDICAL COMPLICATIONS OF MY PATIENTS?

Yes, we are a qualified team of doctors and nurses and paramedical staff. We can take care of co existing medical conditions like diabetes, hypertension&. visiting specialist like gastroenterologists and neurologists are also available if required. If the blood test examination indicates medical complications like varices (bleeding from mouth), jaundice, pancreatitis or any life threatening complication family is advised to shift patient to a multi specialty hospital.

DOES THIS PROGRAM CATER TO THE MENTAL PROBLEMS OF MY PATIENT?

Yes, we are a experienced team of psychiatrist with special training in co occurring psychiatric ailments like schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, anxiety, depression &. Medicines are started for these patients after evaluating their mental status and program is devised to take care of addiction and mental illness.

WHAT IS THE ROLE OF THE FAMILY?

Family has the most important role in the treatment, they can steer the treatment in a positive direction by being honest, committed and sincere. The disease of addiction is a very manipulative; patient knowingly or unknowingly can blackmail their families, so the family should be mentally prepared and discuss the treatment openly and honestly with their therapists.

contentHtml:
Careers

Rehabilitation psychology is a branch of psychology that emphasizes on treating individuals struggling with disorders and issues that make leading normal lives difficult. Professionals in this field try to help patients skirmishing with such problems, in order for the patients to adjust and work towards leading happy and rewarding lives.

This area of psychology often involves treating a broad range of problems. Some of the troubles that clinical psychologists treat may be psychological, and they may include such ailments as depression, anxiety, OCD, schizophrenia, Bipolar Disorder and mental disabilities. Other problems that psychologists treat might be physical, such as addiction. Problems that rehabilitation psychologists treat might be chronic or acute, and they might also be congenital or acquired.

contentHtml:
Treatment of problem drinking at Tulasi Healthcare in Delhi, Gurgaon and India

Tulasi Healthcare offers quality treatment for patients who have drinking problems but are not dependent on alcohol as yet.

Who is a problem drinker?

Problem drinking is 4 times more prevalent in our society than alcoholism.

You may have heard of the term problem drinking and wondered what exactly makes it different from alcoholism. How do you know if you’re a problem drinker or an alcoholic?

Problem drinking is using alcohol in a way that can negatively impact your health and your life, but the body is not physically dependent on alcohol. Alcoholism most likely includes the physical addiction to alcohol in addition to the problems it may cause to your health and to your life.

For instance, a person may be a problem drinker if alcohol causes them to routinely miss work or school, but they can go days, weeks or months without drinking.

An alcoholic usually cannot go a long period of time without needing to drink alcohol but due to the excessive consumption of alcohol, problem drinkers face problems in all spheres of life, both personal & professional.

You may be a problem drinker if alcohol:

  • Makes you miss important functions like class or work.
  • Causes you to avoid family or friends and become isolated.
  • Makes you feel depressed, angry or violent.
  • Causes you to spend money you don’t have and creates financial troubles.
  • Disrupts your relationships with family and friends.
  • Causes you to do something illegal and get arrested due to your behavior.
  • Causes driving under the influence.
  • Causes blackouts.

Risk factors

Family history of alcohol use disorder and inheriting certain genes predispose drinking problems.

Alcohol abuse is common in people older than 65 years of age. It is more dangerous since they are already on prescription medicines which in-turn can adversely react with alcohol & mental illnesses such as depression & anxiety. Problem drinkers are people who drink moderately, heavily or indulge in binge drinking

Moderate drinking:

Moderate drinkers are healthy people who are at low risk of developing an alcohol problem.

  • Women: No more than one drink per day
  • Men: No more than two drinks per day
  • People 65 and older: No more than one drink per day

Even moderate drinking is known to cause problems

  • if alcohol is consumed too quickly,
  • if there is a history of taking certain medication or
  • if there are other health problems.

Heavy drinking:

Heavy drinkers have a very high risk of developing alcohol problems.

  • Women: More than seven drinks per week or three drinks per occasion
  • Men: More than 14 drinks per week or four drinks per occasion

Binge drinking (generally within about two hours):

  • Women: Four or more drinks
  • Men: Five or more drinks

Binge drinkers are usually at risk of developing an alcohol problem. Binge drinkers often do not drink for long periods altogether but once they start they are unable to stop. Gradually their alcohol binge periods become longer and the intake of alcohol also increases.

How to diagnose a drinking problem?

Three key questions are important for diagnosis of drinking problem

  • Have you lost control of your drinking?
  • Have you developed tolerance or other signs of addiction?
  • Are there problem in your job, relationships or with law due to your drinking.

Consequences of problem drinking:

  • Untimely preventable death
  • Road traffic accidents and trauma
  • Suicide or drowning
  • Liver diseases
  • Cancer of mouth, throat, gullet, liver, etc.

Treatment options

  • Counseling from a trained mental health professional
  • Medication
  • Social support groups

It is highly recommended to seek help from an experienced and qualified mental health professional because reducing the consumption or stopping alcohol consumption suddenly can precipitate life threatening withdrawal symptoms. Opportunely, effective treatment for problem drinking is available at Tulasi Healthcare.

excerpt: What is Depression? Depression is more than just a feeling of being low for a few days. contentHtml:
What is Depression?

Depression is more than just a feeling of being low for a few days. It is a condition that slowly chips away on how you think, feel and go about your life in every day actions. It can impact your work, relationships, your sleep, and even your physical health.

We often imagine it as someone crying, unable to get out of bed and visibly not feeling okay. But sometimes it looks high functioning- able to do all your task and still feeling empty inside. Depression is less about sadness and more about disconnection – from yourself, from the things you want enjoyed and from the people who matter. 

At Tulasi Healthcare, many people come in thinking that they just need to go through it and it is just a phase. The first thing people usually take is going online and researching for depression treatment near me. That comes usually from a space of feeling confused, exhausted, or simply feeling that you want to feel better again.

Symptoms of Depression to Watch Out For

Depression is not always something that looks like it is feeling sad. Sometimes, it may feel that you are not going through anything at all. People feel a sense of being numb, they sometimes also like motivation and tend to feel that they are disconnected from everything around them.

For others, it may show up as constant, overthinking, guilt or feeling that things would never get better.

If you’re looking for some common signs to refer to, these include-

  • – Losing interest activities that you enjoyed a lot
  • – Feeling tired, even after ample rest
  • – Changes in sleep patterns – either too much or too little
  • – Difficulty focusing and making decisions
  • – Feeling, hopeless, stuck or overwhelmed

In some cases, people also come to experience physical symptoms like headaches, body aches or heavy feeling in the chest without having any clear medical reason for it

These are the signs that build slowly over time, which are often ignored as one-off issues in the beginning. 

Why do People Delay Getting the Help they Need?

Recognizing depression may seem easy, but it is truly a difficult task. Many people believe that it is just stress, a rough face or something that will go away on its own. Many believe that the stigma around it will not allow them to live in peace within their community, or the fear of being judged comes in between.

At Tulasi Healthcare, it is common to hear people say that they had visited us earlier. The truth is, seeking help is not a sign of your weakness. It is a step towards understanding what is actually the root cause of the problems that you are facing.

If you have been searching for depression treatment in Gurgaon or Delhi NCR, it usually means that you already are aware of some of the problems in your life which need attention.

What Causes Depression?

Depression is not a result of a single point of issue . It can result from an interaction between different types of emotional, psychological, and biological factors.

Some common triggers can include –

– long-term, stress and burnout

– Life changes which are major in case of a loss, separation, or job pressures

– Unresolved experiences

– Family history of mental health concerns

– Chemical imbalances of the brain

And sometimes there is no clear reason at all. Which can also be confusing – but also reminds us that depression is always logical or predictable.

Types of Depression

Not all depression feels the same. There are different types of patterns, intensities and Pritam’s in which it can show up and it can be very difficult to recognise.

  • – Major Depression – It is a deeper, more persistent, and very deep seated, low mood that affects daily functioning –  mood, work, relationships, and even basic routines.
  • – Persistent Depressive Disorder – Acquired, long-term heaviness that stays for years and is mistaken for a personality trait.
  • – Seasonal Depression – In this one, the mood shifts that come also go along with the seasons, often dipping during cold and dark months.
  • – Postpartum Depression – Emotional lows that follow childbirth, which go beyond the expected issues of new parenthood.
  • – Situational Depression – It is triggered by specific life events like loss of a loved one, break up or major change in life.
  • – High Functioning Depression – When everything looks fine from the outside – but there is a single constant problem or struggle that does not let the person having this kind of depression. Stay happy or content for a long time.

How Depression Affects Daily Life

What makes depression difficult to deliver is how it quietly impacts every day functioning. Tasks that once spelt simple – like getting out of bed, replying to messages of focusing at work – can start to feel very overwhelming for people.

You may find yourself withdrawing from situations and people, avoiding your everyday responsibilities, and feeling disconnected even in your most comfortable spaces. Relationships may feel very hard to sustain and productivity also drops. Adding to the feelings of frustration in guilt, everything seems to be very overwhelming for you.

This is where early support becomes a ray of hope. Addressing depression at the right time can help you from affecting multiple areas of life.

When should You Seek Professional Help?

It is very difficult to handle everything on your own and things can really become exhausting. You do not have to see and feel things all by yourself. When you are feeling that you deserve to be understood and not just manage your life – that is where professional help makes sense. It is a space where you do not have to filter, explain and you can just be yourself.

Early support can really prevent things from going bad and become overwhelming overtime. Therapy is not just about fixing what is wrong, but it is also about learning good ways to cope and respond to take care of yourself.

Treatment Options for Depression in Gurgaon & Delhi NCR

Depression is quite treatable, and that is good news. With the right support and understanding, people do recover – and they gain a sense of balance that they never had before.

At Tulasi Healthcare, treatment is not just about taking your symptoms in consideration and treating them till they go away. It is about understanding your experiences, taking them out from the root cause and identifying patterns while helping you cope from them in the healthiest manner possible.

Treatment may include –

  • – Therapy sessions where people can talk openly in safe spaces
  • – Medication, if required to help manage severe symptoms
  • – Lifestyle guidance to improve sleep, routine, and overall well-being
  • – Family support when required to create a better recovery environment

Each individual receives a personalized plan. What works for one person may not be very efficient for the other. It gives you a space where you don’t have to filter yourself out.

1. Psychotherapy / Talk Therapy

One of the most helpful treatments with depression over time is therapy. It gives you a place where you don’t have to filter your thoughts and pretend that you are alright and have everything under control.

Over time, therapy helps you in-

  • – Delving into your emotions, better and deeper
  • – Recognising patterns in your thinking and behaviour
  • – Look for better coping strategies
  • – Improve your relationship with yourself and people around you

Not many people who look for depression treatment near me are looking just for solutions– but they are looking for someone who can listen to them and actually provide a nonjudgemental space for their thoughts. This is exactly what therapy offers.

2. Medication

Medication is not always prescribed. It comes in action when an individual is facing severe symptoms and their therapy and other modalities cannot be completed due to their issues with the symptoms to control it, medications are often prescribed. 

For engaging in daily activities and maintaining a routine to follow therapy, this is essential. It is not necessary for all to have medication, and it is truly upon the condition of the person and the evaluation of a psychiatrist for medication to be prescribed. At Tulasi Healthcare, medication is prescribed only after proper assessment and is always monitored to ensure that it suits your needs.

3. Holistic Therapies

Depression often narrows everything into what is inside our heads. Holistic therapy expands our view here. It understands that depression can also live in the body – as heaviness, low energy and disconnection. It is usually inside our very daily habits that shape how we feel. So instead of only challenging our thoughts, it also supports our emotional expression, our thoughts and physical care through gentle routines. It is important to ask questions like – Am I resting enough? Am I moving enough? Am I feeling connected to myself? When such questions are asked, it becomes very important for us to answer them. Therapy is like mindfulness based therapies, motivational interviewing are really big help.

4. Support Systems

What is having the right support is not about the right words, but not having anything to hide? In depression, even simple days can look heavy and doing them alone is not a good idea. A support system can be a friend who checks in, a family member who sits with you, or a therapist who help you make sense of what feelings you are going through. Sometimes it is just someone reminding you to take care of yourself. At Tulasi Healthcare, we make sure that you receive an amalgamation of all these support systems.

5. Stress Management

What is management stress during depression is not about doing more, but doing things more gently? Our team of experts here at Tulasi Healthcare, help you understand how managing stress can have a positive effect on managing your depression. Starting with grounding techniques and helping you create small routines are the most simplest ways – but the most time taking and effective ones.

Depression can strip away a lot of good things from your life. But it does not mean that you have to be stuck at one place and stay there. With the right support – things can change.

If you are reading this, and recognising that some of them may be present in your life or in the life of your loved ones– it is assigned to take action. Even a small step – like speaking to a professional can start a positive chain of events.

You don’t have to figure everything out on your own. At Tulasi Healthcare, help is available. Whether you have quietly been struggling or actively searching for depression treatment near me, what matters is that you take the next step when you are ready.

Choosing the Right Place for Depression Care

If you have been searching for depression treatment in Gurgaon or Delhi NCR, finding the right place can become a big task if you are not aware about things and how they work. It really matters if you find a team of people who actually care about you, and make a place free of judgement and discomfort so that you can focus on your healing. At Tulasi Healthcare, the approach is very simple – listen first, understand deeply and then guide step-by-step. The focus is always in creating an environment that feels very natural and supportive to you.

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

FAQ's

Which is the best treatment for depression?

There is always an amalgamation of different modalities for depression. There is not one single method that can have a profound effect on a person's depression journey. For the best treatment plan going ahead in the long-term, a mix of all therapy like therapeutic interference and medication along with holistic therapy and support systems is the essential mix for having the right treatment.

Who should one talk to when depressed?

Firstly, people usually approach their family members or their very close people. Whenever they feel distressed or they feel that they are suffering through something. If they are not getting the right kind of support or understanding from the people around them, it is essential that you approach your psychiatrist near you. Try to search up for a psychiatrist near me and approach the best expert near you.

How can I find a psychiatrist for depression near me?

You can easily find a psychiatrist for depression near you. It is important to understand that you go through all the pointers that make a psychiatrist good for your problems. That is you understand, list your problems, find the best matching expert according to your problem and book an appointment easily through an internet search or approach the facility directly.

What are the signs of major depression?

In major depression, people usually feel a very deep seated sense of numbness, isolation, and they always feel like they are not able to continue with any kind of work. They are feeling a reduction in their activity as well as not being able to maintain any kind of work, relationship, and social relations around them. To understand if your loved one is going through such a problem, you can approach your psychiatrist in Gurgaon or Delhi NCR for a quick consultation.

Can depression be treated without medication?

Yes, there is a fair chance that depression can be treated without medication. Given that the condition is diagnosed early on and therapy can easily cover all the bases. But in case the symptoms are severe and the individual is feeling consumed by all the problems that come with depression, medication is essential to control the symptoms.

Is it possible to fully recover from depression?

Yes, it is possible to fully recover from depression. It also depends on the right of factors that people follow through with the treatment thoroughly and maintain their coping strategies in a very honest manner. They should also be ready to catch up with their psychiatrist from time to time in order to maintain a long-term assessment and coping strategy. CONTACT US

contentHtml:
Family Therapy in India & Family Counselling in Delhi, Gurgaon

What is Family Therapy in Psychology & Why family counselling is important?

Substance abuse disorder does not affect just one individual, but affects the entire family of the individual.

Substance abuse disorder does not affect just one individual, but affects the entire family of the individual.

At Tulasi’s Psychiatric Hospital & Rehabilitation Centres, Family Therapy is designed to promote the well-being of those who are struggling with addictions or some other mental disorder and in turn to help their families. Through education and guidance, the family of the patient learns that they can’t control their loved ones’ addiction, but can take responsibility for their own health and happiness.

The stress of living with someone addicted to alcohol or drugs can have physical, emotional, social, and spiritual consequences. Families of alcoholics and addicts often feel confused, frustrated, angry and helpless. Family Therapy helps in alleviating anxiety and also promotes healing by identifying how addiction affects families and what family members can do, to take better care of themselves.

Loved ones of those struggling with addiction must be made aware of the following facts:
  • They can’t control addiction,
  • they didn’t cause addiction and that
  • they can’t cure addiction.

By becoming aware of the beliefs and experiences that shape their own behaviors, participants identify new, healthy ways of coping with addiction and relationships.

The therapy for family involves:
  • Understanding the disease of addiction and its impact on your addicted loved one and on the loved one’s family
  • Learning about the adverse effects of alcohol, tobacco and drug use on your addicted relative’s development and relationships.
  • Developing new techniques for parenting a young blood-relative or someone you care for in recovery
  • Gaining support through interaction with other families, and realizing the benefits of establishing a support network

Planning for continued assistance in the self-care and recovery of the kin or dear one.

What is Family Therapy Counselling for Addiction?

Addictions can feel like they are deeply personal issues, and people with addictions do not want to expose these issues to their families. What they are unaware of, however, is that loved ones can see through their façade and want to help them through this difficult situation.

What Can Counselling Offer the Families?

If the family decides that participating in counselling together with your loved one will be the most beneficial to the lives of all persons affected, you may wonder how it will directly benefit you. The most important part of counselling is not that just the person with an addiction who is supported, but that the family can work out their problems with this situation also.
Family counselling offers the group a safe space to speak about their thoughts, feelings, and concerns. It becomes difficult in personal settings to discuss these feelings without having someone feel like a target. But with fully trained family therapy counsellors mediating these discussions, this will be avoided.

An open family discussion will allow each other to see how they are being affected by these issues. When someone other than yourself is dealing with addiction issues, many prefer to suffer in silence instead of communicating their thoughts. Family therapy activities for communication are usually suggested for such patients.

It is important to know that others feel the same way you do, and know that your worries are supported and not being ignored. The ratio of staff members to counselling clients will always be heavier in favour of the centre, to ensure the amount of support necessary for the family is possible.

By dealing with addiction not as an inherently personal issue, but as something that affects the entire family, everyone’s thoughts and concerns are confronted. Personal development will happen not only for the person with addiction but for everyone.

Through participating in family therapy counselling sessions, each member will come away feeling more understood, more supported, and in turn, become stronger together than they were apart. This is certainly something that families dealing with addiction should take advantage of.

Why Support from and to the Family is Important?

As a disease, addiction’s effects are not limited to the individuals who are trying to recover from it. The family is also put in a lot of stress because of addiction. Persons with addiction problems need to be assisted into recovery. Their families also need help in overcoming this crisis as well.

Family members may begin by learning as much as they can about how they can help their loved one overcome addiction. When more concerned family members are involved and learn about addiction, then they will be better equipped to guide the person with addiction problems to recovery successfully. It is normal for family members to feel hurt, angry, and fearful of what may become of their loved one with an addiction. Most families fear that the addiction can consume the life of their loved one and eventually take it. That’s why family therapy counselling is important for everyone involved.

This person-centric care is built on a shared vision that is established by the family therapy counselor or family therapy psychologist and individual in treatment. Through a collaborative partnership, the counselor and the client discover and nurture ways to build a drug-free life.

Family interventions exist to:

  1. Improve outcomes for the person with the disorder or illness by improving family engagement and effectiveness in handling the challenges associated with the problem.
  2. Improve the well-being of the caregiver as well to reduce stress and negative outcomes of caregiving.
  3. Psychologists can utilize general family interventions with families who are in a caregiving situation and all of the family may benefit.

contentHtml:
TREATMENT OF OBSESSIVE COMPULSIVE DISORDER (OCD) in Delhi & Gurgaon

Obsessive compulsive disorder is a very long blasting and problematic disorder in which a person cannot gain control over their reacquiring thoughts and behaviours. Commonly known as obsessions and compulsions, these provide the name to the disorder and the urge to satisfy them again and again is a very big issue for such people.

People with OCD can have either compulsion or obsessions or both in their behaviour. It can interfere with different aspects of life and render them non-functional in most cases. Areas such as work, school and personal relationships suffer a lot because of the issues it poses.

Obsessions in common terms can be defined as urges, thoughts, or certain mental images that a person feels and thinks about repetitively.

Compulsions on the other hand can be defined as the response of the person towards such urges or mental images.

Not all rituals are compulsions or obsessions as we might think. It is in human nature to think about certain things more than twice or thrice. But it does not qualify as obsessive or compulsive behaviour. In most cases.

Let’s look at what a person with OCD might generally do –

– Spend more than one hour day in indulging in thoughts and behaviours that are repetitive

– Cannot seem to control their thoughts or behaviours, even after being quite aware about them

– Does not get pleasure after completing the behaviour or obsession once or twice and feel the need to repeat it again and again

– Loses their functionality of daily life in order to complete their behaviours

If left untreated or undiagnosed, OCD can be a very problematic situation to be in-  both for the client and their loved ones. If you feel that you will love one sweet professional understanding of their situation, approach Tulasi, psychiatric Hospital and rehab rehabilitation Centre right away.

Symptoms of Obsessive Compulsive Disorder

There are certain levels of symptoms that can be identified to attain a clear picture of OCD. Let’s look at the symptoms in a proper manner.

Symptoms of Obsession in OCD

– Fear of Contamination– This includes a very persistent fear of contamination by germs or fear of getting dirty. This causes obsessive behaviours like frequent hand washing, cleaning, or avoiding certain places that might be prone to these problems.

– Harmful Thought Intrusion– The person has unwanted thoughts of harming others or themselves without any cause.  This can lead to some behaviours that may be pointing towards harm or avoiding certain situations

– Fear of Losing Safety– The person fear that they might lose control over themselves any time which can lead to compulsive behaviours to maintain control over themselves and others.

– Sexual Obsessions– Such people usually get obsessive thoughts about sexual activity or any other thought, which can lead to intense feeling of shame and guilt.

– Religious or Moral Obsessions– there are persistent doubts about one’s morality and religious beliefs, which a person aims to avoid and the behaviours are aimed at finding assurance in their beliefs.

Symptoms of Compulsions in OCD

– Excessive Cleaning or Hand Washing– such individuals feel a very excessive need to clean their hands, or they feel that they are plagued by germs and need to get rid of them as soon as possible.

– Checking Behaviours– with a doubt in their minds, such people always check the locks and appliances more than the required amount and they feel that they might get harmed and have safety related concerns.

– Performing Mental Rituals– such people often pray or repeat certain words in order to avoid harm repetitively.

– Ordering or Arranging Objects– such people need to maintain symmetry and order, and in this way, they feel related to the outcomes of their actions. 

– Hoarding or Collect– when people feel a persistent need to keep or collect objects without having the need to do it.

What are the Causes Behind Obsessive Compulsive Disorder?

The exact causes behind compulsive disorder are not fully understood, but it is a mix of factors that bring about its onset. Let’s explore some factors that we contribute to the development of this disorder-

– Genetic Factors– OCD appears to be present in families for generations, suggesting a genetic component to its development. Some induct studies in such factors from that a lot of jeans might be involved in the development and onset of this disorder.

– Neurological Factors– there might be some abnormalities present in certain parts of the brain that can cause this issue. These parts include orbitofrontal cortex, anterior cingulate cortex, and basal ganglia, which are some areas that have been seen to be associated with OCD in general. Since these areas are responsible for regulating behaviour and emotions, they seem to play a big part in individual OCD being underactive or overactive.

– Environmental Factors– traumatic and stressful life events can trigger the onset of OCD. Events like abuse, illness, or loss of a loved one have usually been seen to contribute to the onset and development of OCD in some individuals. Apart from this, many infections and autoimmune disorders can also contribute to OCD in some people.

– Cognitive Factors– since people with OCD have a certain pattern of thinking like perfection or more heightened sense of responsibility,  it can trigger a sense of compulsions and obsessions. 

It is important to note that obsessive compulsive disorder is a very complex condition that can be triggered by any of these factors or a combination of these in any proportion. Treatment in the long run can help manage symptoms and improve functionality and quality of life.

Types of Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD)

Obsessive compulsive disorder can also be of many types which can seem to show certain patterns and themes of onset. Some common types of OCD include-

– Contamination OCD–  Here, the person is plagued with the fear of contamination of germs, dirt or any other pathogen. This leads to excessive hand washing, cleaning of oneself and surfaces and avoidance of places and objects that  increase probability of contamination.

–Checking OCD– it is a fear of harm and danger that leads people to check excessively on things that are responsible for their safety. Locks and appliances are under constant supervision.

–Symmetry OCD– such people feel that everything should be kept in order and in a symmetrical manner. If not done, it can lead to compulsive behaviours as well as unwanted outcomes and situations.

–Hoarding OCD– people with this OCD feel very difficult to part with their positions and Dis, kindly to excessive clutter and keeping things without any need. This interferes with their daily functioning as well.

–Sexual or Religious OCD– obsessions referred to sexual and religious themes come under this category. Such obsessions lead to feelings of shame and guilt and only compulsive behaviours can reduce anxiety.

It’s important to consider that these OCDs are not mutually exclusive. It can occur in moderation or be present in multiple types. To understand what is going on with your loved ones, it is important to see professional help.

Treatment Modalities for Obsessive Compulsive Disorder

OCD is typically treated with medication, psychotherapy or a combination of different modalities. Most of the patients see considerable improvement with medication and therapy. However, there is a very small population that may require brain stimulation techniques for immediate effect.

Comorbidities with OCD also show up in the form of depression, anxiety, and other disorders like body dysmorphia.

Medication Modalities– Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) are very effective in reducing OCD symptoms. Medications have always been proved effective with adults and children with OCD. 

Within 8 to 12 weeks, the treatment for OCD starts to show effect with medication and regular therapeutic management. If symptoms do not improve with medication, some people also respond well to Anti- psychotic medication.

Psychotherapy– psychotherapy can be a very good mode of treatment for adults and children with OCD. Certain types like cognitive behavioural therapy, habit reversal training and exposure and response prevention therapy are some of the most effective ones in people who are not able to respond well to SRI medication. 

Finding the Right Treatment Plan for You

At Tulasi Healthcare, we believe that support and hope are the pillars of a good support system. As your support system towards a life of health and functional well-being, we offer effective treatment plans by obsessive compulsive disorder. Connect with us today in any form to know how we can be of help. 

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

FAQ's

What are the common symptoms of OCD?

The common symptoms of OCD include repetitive behaviors or mental acts, such as excessive cleaning, counting, checking, or arranging, that interfere with daily life; unwanted, intrusive, or distressing thoughts, images, or impulses that are difficult to control; and anxiety, fear, or guilt related to the obsessions and compulsions.

What causes OCD?

The exact cause of OCD is not known, but it is believed to be related to a combination of genetic, environmental, and neurobiological factors. Studies suggest that changes in the brain's circuitry and chemistry may play a role in the development of OCD.

How is OCD diagnosed?

OCD is diagnosed based on the presence of obsessions and compulsions that cause significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of functioning. A mental health professional, such as a psychiatrist or psychologist, may use interviews, questionnaires, and other assessment tools to diagnose OCD.

What are the treatment options for OCD?

The treatment options for OCD include medication, such as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), and psychotherapy, such as cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) and exposure and response prevention (ERP) therapy. A combination of medication and therapy may be more effective for some people.

Can OCD be cured?

There is no known cure for OCD, but it can be effectively managed with treatment. Many people with OCD experience significant improvement in their symptoms with medication and/or therapy. It is important to seek treatment as soon as possible to prevent the condition from worsening and interfering with daily life. Contact us Contact Us

contentHtml:
Tulasi Healthcare Bipolar Disorder Treatment Centre in Gurgaon and Delhi NCR

An Overview of Bipolar Disorder

Bipolar Disorder or manic depression is a chronic mood disorder characterized by large shifts in mood, energy, activity levels, and concentration of an individual leading to irritability and impulsive or reckless decision-making.

People suffering from this mental illness have periods in which they feel overly happy and at other periods feel sad, sluggish and hopeless. In between these periods, these people feel normal. These periods of high and low are treated as two poles of mood and thus it is popularly called as bipolar disorder.

Bipolar disorder is prevalent among individuals aged between 20 and 30 years and affects anywhere from 0.5 to 21 out of every 1000 Indians annually. Out of 150 individuals suffering from this mental illness, 70% left untreatable. Although this mental disorder is a lifelong condition, good medical care, lifestyle changes, psychological counselling (psychotherapy) at Gurgaon can make a huge difference.

Symptoms of Bipolar Disorder

The most distinguishing symptoms of bipolar disorder are highs or lows in mood, coupled with changes in energy/ activity levels, sleep, thinking as well as behaviour. The three major symptoms that features this disorder are mania, hypomania, and depression. An individual may suffer from different types of bipolar disorder based on different combinations of these symptoms

Bipolar I Symptoms

Diagnosis of Bipolar I requires:

  • One episode of mania that should last for atleast a week.
  • Symptoms affecting daily activity of an individual.
  • Symptoms that are not related to any other medical and mental health condition.

At times individuals may experience symptoms of psychosis or both mania and depression (known as mixed features).

Bipolar II Symptoms

Diagnosis of Bipolar II requires:

  • One episode of hypomania that should last for 4 days or more.
  • Change in mood and usual function of an individual due to hypomania that can be noticed by others.
  • One episode of major depression that should last for 2 weeks or more.
  • One episode of major depression that involves one or more key depression symptoms significantly impacting day to day activity of an individual.
  • Symptoms that are not related to any other medical and mental health condition.

At times individuals can show symptoms of psychosis, but only during an episode of depression while at other times they can experience mixed mood episodes, which is a combination of depression and hypomania.

Cyclothymia Symptoms

Diagnosis of Cyclothymia requires:

  • Periods of depression symptoms and periods of hypomanic symptoms, on and off that should last for 2 years or more.
  • Symptoms that do not fulfil the full criteria of an episode of depression or hypomania.
  • Symptoms that are available for atleast half of the 2 years and is never absent for more than 2 months.
  • Symptoms that are not related to any other medical and mental health condition.
  • Symptoms causing significant distress and affecting daily life.

Fluctuating mood is a major symptom of cyclothymia. Though cyclothymia may be less severe than Bipolar I/ II, they tend to last longer.

Hypomania usually does not have a major impact on an individual’s daily life while depression may lead to more serious distress and affects day-to-day activity of an individual.

Common symptoms of mania ("the highs"):

  • Excessive hopefulness, happiness, and excitement.
  • Restlessness.
  • Sudden change in being joyful to being angry, irritable, and hostile.
  • Poor concentration
  • Enhanced energy level leading to less sleep.
  • Exceptionally high sex drive.
  • Demonstrating poor judgement.
  • Alcohol and drug abuse.
  • Impulsive behaviour.
  • Less appetite
  • Boost in self-confidence and well being
  • Easy distraction.

Common symptoms of depression ("the lows"):

  • Feeling of sadness
  • Loss in energy level
  • Feelings of worthlessness or hopelessness
  • Poor concentration
  • Loss of memory
  • To talk slowly
  • Decrease in sex drive
  • Trouble in taking decision
  • Crying in uncontrollable manner
  • Insomnia
  • Loss/ Gain in appetite
  • Though of suicide attempt or death

What are the causes of Bipolar Disorder?

Though the exact cause of bipolar disorder has not yet been identified, studies have shown that bipolar disorder is seen more in women compared to men due to medical and mental issues that may include migraine, thyroid disease, and anxiety disorders. Factors contributing to bipolar disorder are as follows:

Brain structure and functioning: Studies have shown that people suffering from bipolar disorder have brains that differ in certain ways from normal individual. Thus healthcare providers carry diagnosis and treatment based on a person’s symptoms and history, instead of brain imaging or other diagnostic tests.

Genetics: Family (parent or sibling) history plays a significant role in developing bipolar disorder in individuals. Studies have shown that individuals with certain genes are more likely to develop this mental disorder.

Environment: Environment can also contribute to the development of bipolar disorder in individuals. Extreme stress, traumatic experiences and physical illness can invite bipolar disorder in a healthy human being.

Treatment options available for Bipolar Disorder at Tulasi Healthcare

In most cases, bipolar disorder is non-curable but various treatments and therapies help reduce symptoms of this medical illness. At Tulasi Psychiatric Hospital & Rehabilitation Centers, Bipolar treatment in delhi & gurgaon consists:

  • Medication
  • Counselling by recognized counsellor
  • Change in lifestyle

Bipolar Disorder Medications

Common medications for this disorder are:

  • Mood stabilizers: In most cases, lithium (Lithobid) is used for mood stabilization. In this approach, use of these medicines is not to be paired with the consumption of alcohol or consumption of water. In addition, Psychiatrist also prescribes a renal function test on case-to-case basis. Some other tests include thyroid and an annual ECG.
  • Antipsychotics: In most cases, olanzapine (Zyprexa) is used to treat psychotic symptomssuch as hallucinations, or delusions that may accompany severe depression or mania. Sometimes, such medicines are also prescribed to treat other symptoms such as anxiety.
  • Antidepressant: In most cases, fluoxetine-olanzapine (Symbyax) is used to treat depressive episodes in bipolar disorder.
  • anti-anxiety medication for short term treatment, namely benzodiazepines

Psychotherapy for Bipolar Disorder Treatment

Recommended approaches are given below:

Cognitive behavioral therapy

This is a talk therapy that helps individual change unwanted behavior patterns and identify and address unhelpful thoughts. Some of the supports which therapists offer are:

  • Undertaking thought pattern of an individual suffering from this disorder.
  • Reframe distressing emotions
  • Learn and practise helpful coping strategies

Psychoeducation

This is a therapeutic approach to help an individual learn about a condition and its treatment. This knowledge can have a long term effect helping an individual and the supporting people in his/ her life recognize mood symptoms and managing those effectively.

Interpersonal and social rhythm therapy

In this approach, more indulgence is given to regulate the daily habits of an individual such as eating, sleeping, exercising, etc. A balance among these daily activities could lead to lesser mood swings and less severe symptoms.

Apart from the above approaches Tulasi Health Care’s team of rehabilitation experts also suggest few lifestyle changes that can help reduce symptoms of bipolar disorder.

Lifestyle changes to help Bipolar Disorder

Some simple changes in an individual’s lifestyle can help deal with bipolar disorder. Few of these are given below:

  • Maintaining a balanced diet.
  • Maintaining a schedule for eating and sleeping
  • Regular exercise
  • Learn recognizing mood swings
  • Learn managing stress
  • Avoid consumption of alcohol or recreational drugs
  • Engage in healthy hobbies or sports
FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

FAQ's

How is bipolar disorder diagnosed?

A mental health professional, such as a psychiatrist or psychologist, can diagnose bipolar disorder based on a person's symptoms and history. They may also conduct a physical exam and run tests to rule out any medical conditions that could be causing the symptoms.

What causes bipolar disorder?

The exact cause of bipolar disorder is not fully understood, but it is believed to be a combination of genetic, environmental, and neurobiological factors. Having a family history of bipolar disorder or other mental health conditions can increase the risk of developing the disorder.

What is bipolar disorder treatment?

Bipolar disorder is typically treated with a combination of medication, such as mood stabilizers and antipsychotics, and psychotherapy, such as cognitive-behavioral therapy and interpersonal therapy. Lifestyle changes, such as getting regular exercise, maintaining a healthy diet, and managing stress, can also be helpful.

Can people with bipolar disorder live normal lives?

Yes, with proper treatment and management, many people with bipolar disorder are able to lead fulfilling lives. However, it is important to continue treatment even during periods of stability to prevent relapses.

Is bipolar disorder the same as depression?

No, bipolar disorder is not the same as depression. While depression is a component of bipolar disorder, people with bipolar disorder also experience episodes of mania or hypomania.

Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT)

The central goal of cognitive behavioural therapy is to teach the patient to deal with situations in which they are most likely to abuse substances, to avoid these circumstances and to cope with other behavioural changes. Cognitive behavioural therapy is comprised of two main components-

  • Functional Analysis
  • Skills Training

At our drug and alcohol rehabilitation centre in Delhi, we have included both main components for the therapy to get rid of addiction.
The therapist and the patient try to identify the thoughts and circumstances of the patients before and after they abused the substance(s). This helps the patient determine the risks that are likely to lead to a relapse. Unlike other substance de-addiction centers in Delhi, Gurgaon  Tulasi implements the most appropriate treatment methods for affected people. Tulasi Health Care’s de-addiction center offers a customized psychotherapy program to meet an individual’s exclusive needs.

Functional Analysis:

We strongly believe that it is possible to de addict from alcohol, smoking and any substance’s use when one wins over his/her thoughts. Working together, the therapist and the patient try to identify the thoughts, feelings and circumstances of the patient before and after they drink or use drugs. This in-turn helps the patient identify the feelings and circumstances which are likely to lead to a relapse. Functional analysis can help the patients gain an insight into why they drink or use drugs and identify situations in which the person has coping difficulties.

Skills Training:

If someone is at a point where he/she needs professional treatment for his/her alcohol or drug dependence, chances are that they are using alcohol or drugs as the main means of coping with their problems. The goal of cognitive behavioral therapy is to get the person to learn or re-learn better coping skills. The therapist tries to help the individual unlearn old habits and learn to develop new, healthier skills and habits. The main goal of cognitive behavior therapy is to educate the alcohol or drug-dependent person to change the way they think about their substance abuse and to learn new ways to cope with the situations and circumstances that led to their drinking or drugging episodes in the past.

contentHtml:
Tulasi Healthcare offers the Best Relapse Prevention strategies for Addiction in India

Recovery from drug or alcohol addiction is a huge accomplishment.

But are you aware that relapse of addiction is a possibility?

There are no miracles that prevent relapse, but constant efforts put in by the addicted individual and his family mitigates the chances of a probable relapse.

Addiction takes its toll on the entire family. While you may be excited to hear that your loved one is ready to end his/her addiction, you may also have valid concerns about whether or not his/her sobriety will last. Relapse is a serious concern for anyone who struggles with addiction, and the right treatment program has solutions that help reduce the chances of your loved one returning to his/her former habit(s).The family too can play a vital role in preventing a relapse.

What is Addiction Relapse?

It is a cardinal feature of addiction which is most painful. It means returning to substance use after a substance-free period. In medical science, a relapse is a return to a heavier usage of drugs and / or alcohol.

Why does it Happen?

  • Addiction disorder is a chronic disorder that cannot be cured but can be managed
  • Drug or alcohol related reminders like sounds, smells, sights, thoughts or even dreams
  • Negative mood states like anxiety, stress etc.
  • Positive mood states like euphoria resulting from celebration, social get-togethers, etc.
  • Prolonged mental illness(es) like bipolar disorder or schizophrenia

Addiction Relapse Prevention

Ideally, after he/she is through with his/her addiction treatment program(s), your loved one should continue with after care services such as counseling and day-care, that helps him/her address issues that arise after they return home. Make sure that your loved one has time to attend these appointments, and do your part to reduce temptation around the house. For instance, you can plan drug and alcohol free activities to do with your loved one to keep them busy. Going for a hike or just watching a movie are great ways to bond and reduce cravings.

Families play a vital role in helping their loved ones overcome addiction. To find more ways that you can help, feel free to connect with us over a phone call.

cognitive behavioural relapse prevention program

Patients can also connect with us for the cognitive behavioural relapse prevention program. It is a process that focuses on lifestyle, behavioural and cognitive changes. It helps develop coping skills to steer clear of addiction.
It elaborates on how to avoid tempting situations, develop a positive support network, create healthy schedules and keeps one busy so as to avoid signs of relapse. We guide via constructive activities like reading, meditation and exercising to prevent relapse.

Contact us to Keep Your Loved Ones Free from Addiction for a Life Time.

contentHtml:
Treatment of Schizophrenia in Delhi, Gurgaon & NCR

Schizophrenia is a mental disorder that affects an individual’s thinking capacity, emotions and behavior pattern(s) to an extent that they seem to have lost contact with the reality. Although schizophrenia is not as common as other mental and behavioral disorders (it affects about 1 in every 100 people during their lifetime), it is a long-term illness and can be extremely disabling. People with symptoms of schizophrenia present complex behavioral and cognitive dysfunctionality, they find it hard to think rationally and may experience unusual things such as hearing strange voices or having false or bizarre beliefs. Tulasi Healthcare is best schizophrenia treatment centre in Gurgaon & NCR. 

Types of Schizophrenia

Following are the types of Schizophrenia Disorder

Paranoid Schizophrenia
Heberprenic Schizophrenia
Catatonic Schizophrenia
Residual Schizophrenia
Simple Schizophrenia
Undifferentiated schizophrenia

Symptoms of Schizophrenia

The complexity of symptoms is typical of schizophrenia. It manifests differently in everyone, which makes it important to consider the specific needs of the patient(s) in order to assist them and plan treatment. The symptomatic trends around it

Positive Symptoms of Schizophrenia -

A person suffering from schizophrenia may experience some thoughts, emotions or indulge into behavior(s) that were not present earlier or are not experienced by people in general. Such symptoms are called positive symptoms. These include:

  • Hallucinations- distorted perception of the things around or perceiving (hearing voices, seeing, smelling or feeling things) when the external stimuli are not present.
  • Delusions- unshakable false beliefs which are different from reality or awkward. Example, a person may have a delusion of others controlling his/her actions and thoughts.
  • Abnormal motor symptoms – catatonia, where the affected person does not move or respond to others; repetitive unusual bodily movements; psychomotor slowing.
  • Thought disorder- disorganized thinking, absurd content and flow of thoughts.

Negative Symptoms of Schizophernia -

Negative symptoms are those thinking, emotional or behavioral aspects of normal functioning that are absent or diminish in person with the disorder. People presenting negative symptoms need support in everyday chores as their functionality is severely affected. These include:

  • Social withdrawal- avoids social engagements or prefers being isolated most of the time.
  • Inability to regulate and express emotions.
  • Lack of motivation or drive.
  • Diminished capacity to experience pleasure.
  • Deteriorating thinking capacity and speech.

Cognitive Symptoms-

A person with schizophrenia experiences the significant disturbance in higher mental functioning. These include:

  • Difficulty in understanding and comprehending information.
  • Inability to focus or sustain attention.
  • Diminished capacity to make decisions.
  • Difficulty in retaining and remembering information- poor memory.

Schizophrenia Diagnosis and Treatment

Considering the complexities of such mental and behavioral disorders, our trained professionals deem in treating patients having psychiatric disorders with care and compassion. Only the experts from the fields of psychiatry & psychology see and assess patient and the family to make a case summary based on which an informed diagnosis is made by experienced Psychiatrist.

Family history and substance abuse related questions are asked from the family members and it is expected of them to provide honest answers to the questions so that treatment procedures go well.

Schizophrenia Treatment in Delhi, Gurgaon & NCR

Schizophrenia may be caused by a combination of genetic and psycho-social (environmental) factors that leads to biochemical imbalances in the brain. At Tulasi Healthcare, we offer schizophrenia treatment in Delhi, Gurgaon And NCR & comprehensive care for persons diagnosed with schizophrenia- medical treatment (pharmacotherapy) and psychosocial rehabilitation (Psychotherapy).

Schizophrenia Medication

Antipsychotic medications for schizophrenia are prescribed in most cases as they regulate the levels of biochemical functions (neurotransmitters) in the brain and control symptoms. Some common side effects of antipsychotic drugs may be:

  • Dizziness
  • Restlessness
  • Weight gain
  • Tremor

Antipsychotic drugs, besides being able to manage current symptoms, are also recommended after treatment to prevent relapse.

Psychosocial Rehabilitation

We firmly believe that psychological intervention combined with medication is essential for effective management of our patients. Our psychosocial rehabilitation program has helped many of our patients with schizophrenia to lead enriched lives. By means of a patient-centered approach, we aim to provide emotional support and motivation to the patients helping them establish a trusting relationship with the therapist that would facilitate their recovery. Psychological interventions with counselling help them restore their self-esteem and self-confidence. Based on the course of illness and specific needs, our expert therapists practice different approaches with patients to bring desired behavioral changes.

The Rehabilitation program at Tulasi rehabilitation centre also includes following group activities focused on the overall psychosocial development of individuals:

Family Education and engagement facilitates the treatment process. Families are educated about the illness, the treatment and how to deal with the patient, including how to behave, maintaining recovery and preventing relapse.

Self-Help

We encourage our patients to become self-dependent in various aspects- such as social skills, self-care which includes the use of public transportation, daily chores and activities, managing their own routine and control over the lifestyle to some extent.

To ensure long-term benefits of the treatment we choose the combination of complementary interventions and approaches that are most favorable to the patient.

Our team of experienced psychiatrists & psychologists for treatment of schizophrenia in Delhi NCR

What is Schizophrenia?

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

FAQ's

When does schizophrenia typically start?

Schizophrenia usually starts in the late teens or early adulthood, although it can develop at any age. It is rare for children to develop schizophrenia disorder.

What are the causes of schizophrenia?

The exact causes of schizophrenia are not known, but researchers believe that a combination of genetic, environmental, and brain chemistry factors may play a role.

Is schizophrenia hereditary?

There is a genetic component to schizophrenia, but it is not entirely hereditary. While people with a family history of schizophrenia are at higher risk of developing the condition, many people with no family history also develop schizophrenia.

How is schizophrenia diagnosed?

Schizophrenia is diagnosed through a comprehensive evaluation that includes a physical exam, lab tests, and a psychiatric evaluation. A doctor or mental health professional will look for symptoms that meet the criteria outlined in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5).

What are the treatment options for schizophrenia?

The main treatments for schizophrenia are antipsychotic medications, psychotherapy, and social and vocational skills training. A combination of these treatments is frequently most effective.

Is there a cure for schizophrenia?

While there is no cure for schizophrenia, many people with the condition are able to manage their symptoms and live fulfilling lives with the help of treatment and support. Recovery is often a lifelong process that involves ongoing treatment and management.

Can people with schizophrenia work or go to school?

Yes, many people with schizophrenia are able to work or go to school with the right treatment and support. Vocational and educational support can be helpful in finding and maintaining employment or education opportunities.

How can family and friends support someone with schizophrenia?

Family and friends can support someone with schizophrenia by providing emotional support, helping them access treatment and support services, and encouraging them to stick to their treatment plan. It can also be helpful to educate oneself about the condition and to be patient and understanding with the person's symptoms and behavior.

contentHtml:
Heroin Rehab Programs

Symptoms and Treatment of Heroin Addiction

Tulasi Healthcare’s heroin addiction treatment centres and marijuana addiction treatment centres in Delhi have been actively working on preventing the onslaught of heroin addiction and on keeping India free from heroin addiction. The Delhi NCR based heroin treatment center has been listed as one of the best heroin addiction treatment centres in India.

Amongst the 7.5 crore drug addicts in India, approximately 1 crore are heroin addicts. The drug is readily available across the country because of the illicit cultivation of opium in Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and many other states of the country, on a large scale. Moreover, it is also smuggled into India from our neighbouring countries like Afghanistan.

What is heroin?

Heroin, also known as diamorphine among other names, is an opioid most commonly used as a recreational drug for its euphoric effects. Medically, it is used in several countries to relieve pain or in opioid replacement therapy. Heroin is typically injected, usually into a vein: however, it can also be smoked, snorted or inhaled. The onset of effects is usually rapid and lasts for a few hours.

Common side effects include dry mouth, drowsiness, impaired mental function, constipation and addiction. Giving up the habit after long-term use, withdrawal symptoms can begin within hours of last usage.

When administered by injection into a vein, heroin has two to three times the effect as of a similar dose of morphine. It typically comes as a white or brown powder.

Symptoms of Addiction

  • Dry mouth and skin
  • Constricted pupils
  • Insomnia
  • Decreased breathing (if heroin is smoked)
  • Itching, vomiting and nausea
  • Mental function impairment
  • Poor performance
  • Regular injection of heroin can cause:
  • abscesses
  • infected heart valves
  • blood borne infections and
  • pneumonia

Risks

Following are the risks associated with regular heroin usage:

  • An overdose of Heroin may prove fatal
  • Physical dependence due to frequent use
  • An overdose may also cause respiratory depression, shallow breathing, hypotension and coma
  • Administering heroin injections intravenously may cause HIV, hepatitis and toxic reactions owing to needles being contaminated
  • Collapsed veins and
  • Endocarditis (inflammation of the heart lining and valves)
  • Liver disease
  • Kidney disease
  • Bacterial infections
  • Organ damage (typically caused by additives in street heroin)

Treatment Options for Heroin Addiction

What you experience during heroin addiction treatment is going to solely depend on specific factors including how long you have been using and how much you have been using?

Your recovery will depend on your ability to understand and cope with other challenges, such as underlying psychological problems which may have been caused by (excessive) heroin usage.

There are two kinds of treatment centers: residential and outpatient.

Heroin is highly addictive to a point, where nearly one-quarter of people who use heroin develop a dependency.

Once addiction has developed, users will stop at nothing to get more of the drug even if it means risking their jobs, damaging relationships with loved ones and more.

However, treatment of heroin addiction is very much possible. Timely diagnosis of addiction-induced diseases and their treatment is beneficial.

Tulasi Healthcare delivers quality treatment by combining medication compliance programs and rehabilitation therapy for reversing and curing heroin addiction.

Our Delhi and Gurgaon-based treatment centre is committed to providing support to addicted individuals throughout the treatment via inpatient or outpatient care programs. For every patient, there is a customized plan of action, which is devised while taking into consideration their symptoms. Our treatment approach is holistic and includes medication, psychotherapy & support groups.

At the beginning of the rehabilitation program, medicines that help mitigate the heroin cravings are administered and later on, during the treatment, behavioural therapy is undertaken to curtail cravings naturally.

At our rehabilitation centres, we make patients engage in social activities. Yoga and meditation are also taught. We try to restore their lifestyles to normalcy and help them in every manner possible to keep addiction and related symptoms at bay. We provide support to family members too, which helps in expediting the recovery process. Also, we remain in touch with the patient after the treatment is over, in order to eliminate the possibility of a relapse.
